title: Token-fingerprint coalescer + idle-window online compaction controller for KV cache
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Persistent KV cache fragmentation is a recurring source of GPU memory waste and increased cold miss amplification for our serving runtime. Existing slab and chunk-based strategies handle steady-state allocation well, but workload skew and token-locality shifts create micro-fragments across GPU memory that degrade effective capacity and force higher model offload/slow-paths under load.

Problem statement:
We need a low-risk, incremental system that: (1) reduces long-tail fragmentation without major synchronous pauses, (2) co-locates frequently-accessed KV entries by request/token locality to improve prefix cache hits, and (3) uses otherwise-idle GPU windows to compact/relocate data while respecting latency SLOs.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a two-part subsystem: 1) Token-fingerprint coalescer: at allocation time, annotate KV entries with a small 8-byte fingerprint derived from request token fingerprinting + route/model context. Use a micro-shard index to place new allocations in affinity groups so that items with similar fingerprints land in the same micro-shard/stripe. This improves locality and reduces scattered small allocations across slabs. 2) Idle-window online compaction controller: a background scheduler that opportunistically performs relocation and compaction during measured low-utilization windows on each GPU. The controller uses asynchronous copy kernels + lightweight metadata updates to avoid blocking inference. Compactions are prioritized by expected space reclaimed and runtime impact.

Design details:
- Fingerprint generation: use a 64-bit xxhash over (model_id, route_id, top- token-prefix hash) folded to 8 bytes. The coalescer evaluates recent token access histograms per-route to determine shard affinity thresholds.
- Micro-shard layout: each large slab is sub-divided into N micro-shards (configurable, default 16). Allocator places small allocations (<= 256B) into the micro-shard chosen by fingerprint % N. Larger KV entries use size-class aware placement but prefer adjacent micro-shards when fingerprint shows strong locality.
- Compaction controller: runs as a per-GPU cooperative coroutine. It monitors three signals: GPU compute utilization, inferred inference tail-latency risk (p95 threshold), and disk/PCIe bandwidth availability. Only when utilization < U_low and tail-latency risk is low will it schedule relocation tasks. Relocation is staged: allocate target region, async memcpy KV payload, atomically swap metadata pointer, mark old region reclaimable. If any memcpy or swap fails or latency risk spikes, cancel and roll back.
- Heuristics and prioritization: prioritize micro-shards with high fragmentation score = (free_gaps > gap_threshold) * expected_reclaimable_bytes / cost_estimate. Also bias toward shards with many small, short-lived entries to avoid moving cold large values.
- Safety and consistency: all pointer swaps are versioned via an epoch counter; readers consult epoch and follow a two-phase read-with-retry when a relocation is in-flight. The controller uses lightweight fencing but avoids global stalls.

Telemetry and acceptance criteria:
- New gauges: micro_shard_fragmentation_ratio, compaction_reclaim_rate_bytes_per_second, compaction_failures_count, avg_compact_window_duration, relocations_per_minute.
- SLO constraints: compaction must not increase p99 inference latency by > 2% in production canaries.
- Target outcomes for rollout: reduce observed fragmentation overhead (wasted bytes due to gaps) by >= 20% on average across benchmark workloads, and reduce inter-request prefix miss rate by >= 8% for skewed prefix workloads.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (Spike, 2 weeks): implement fingerprint generator and micro-shard placement in allocator unit tests + simulator. Add synthetic workloads to verify co-location improves measured local-hit rate.
Phase 2 (Dev, 3 weeks): implement micro-shard layout in runtime with feature flag. Expose telemetry counters. Run internal perf tests on canaries (staging-GPU cluster).
Phase 3 (Compaction, 3 weeks): implement idle-window compaction controller with conservative thresholds + safe rollback. Controlled canary rollout (10% of serving fleet) with shadow compaction enabled first (measure only).
Phase 4 (Rollout, 2 weeks): enable compaction in production for non-critical routes, gradually expand. Tune heuristics.

Testing matrix:
- Unit tests for fingerprint collisions and shard distribution (statistical checks).
- Microbenchmarks: relocation latency, async memcpy throughput under mixed-load.
- End-to-end: canary traffic with AB test measuring latency, cost, and cache hit rates. Include stress tests with oscillating token locality to ensure compaction respects safety constraints.

Rollbacks and mitigation:
Feature gate at runtime plus per-GPU controller throttle. Immediate stop when p95 or p99 latency increases by configured margin. Migration of reclaimable memory happens only after stable epoch; we can mark compaction as dry-run to collect metrics before enabling mutation.

Open questions / risks:
1) Fingerprint stability vs. index drift: Need to pick fingerprint window size (token prefix depth) to balance locality and churn. We will test 8/16/32 token-prefix depths.
2) Extra metadata overhead: micro-shard bookkeeping increases per-entry metadata by ~8–12 bytes. Verify net memory benefit in bench runs.
3) Async copy bandwidth contention: on GPUs with high PCIe usage the compaction could contend; controller must be PCIe-aware.
4) Interactions with existing slab reclamation and generational pools: we must ensure compaction does not cause regressions in current eviction heuristics.

comments: 2026-02-19 - Maya Chen: Spike complete. Fingerprint distribution looks stable on synthetic long-tail workloads; 12% improvement in local-prefix hits in simulator. Added simulator code in kv-sim PR.

2026-02-25 - Arjun Patel: Reviewed spike. Agree on micro-shard approach. Concern: per-entry metadata overhead might offset gains for very small KV footprints. Recommend measuring net effective memory after micro-shard headers in phase 2.
2026-03-03 - Lina Sørensen (SRE): Added note about PCIe contention. Suggest controller sample PCIe BW and avoid compaction if it would push bandwidth > 70% of baseline.

2026-03-08 - Security review (brief): No customer data exfiltration risk observed for fingerprint-only metadata. Ensure fingerprints are non-reversible; use salted hash per-tenant when private deployment is enabled.

2026-03-12 - Performance: Staging canary (2 nodes) shows 22% reduction in fragmentation metric, compaction reclaim rate 40MB/s during idle windows. No measurable latency regression so far (p99 delta +0.6%).

2026-03-14 - Arjun Patel: Implementing phase 2 changes in runtime branch eng/ENG-550123-microshard. Opened PR 2106 for allocator placement. Next: integrate compaction controller skeleton and add telemetry counters.
